content: Infants under the age of 12 months have been associated with adverse outcomes related to the use of cough and cold medications. Medical examiners or coroners have determined these medications to be the underlying cause of death in certain cases. These findings emphasize the importance of clinicians exercising caution when prescribing, and caregivers being vigilant when administering, cough and cold medications to children under the age of 2 years. Guaifenesin works by thinning mucus in the airways, making it easier to cough up and clear the air passages, thereby improving breathing. It is effective in relieving coughs caused by colds, bronchitis, and other respiratory infections. In some cases, guaifenesin may be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for further information. Guaifenesin is available in various forms, including regular and extended-release tablets, capsules, and liquid formulations, all intended for oral administration. Follow the instructions on the package or prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take guaifenesin exactly as directed. Do not take more or less than prescribed, and do not take it more frequently than instructed. Extended-release tablets should not be broken, crushed, or chewed, and extended-release capsules should not be opened; they must be swallowed whole. Ensure adequate fluid intake while taking this medication unless otherwise directed by your doctor. Guaifenesin is available as a standalone medication or in combination with antihistamines, cough suppressants, and decongestants. Consult your doctor or pharmacist to determine the most appropriate formulation for your symptoms. If your symptoms do not improve within 7 days, or if you experience a high fever, rash, or persistent headache, contact your doctor. Before taking guaifenesin, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to guaifenesin or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, including vitamins, that you are currently taking. Notify your doctor if you have a history of high blood pressure, heart disease, thyroid disorders, or diabetes. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking guaifenesin, contact your doctor immediately. If you miss a dose of guaifenesin, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Guaifenesin may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: headache, upset stomach, or vomiting. Store guaifenesin in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any expired or no longer needed medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on the appropriate disposal of medications. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
